- [USER] User expressed interest in the impact of the Venice Biennale on the global art world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Venice Biennale is one of the most prestigious and oldest international art exhibitions in the world, taking place every other year in Venice, Italy, showcasing contemporary art from around the globe.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The impact of the Venice Biennale on the global artistic community is significant, providing a platform for emerging and established artists to showcase their work, network, and receive critical feedback.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Biennale serves as a hub for art dealers, museum directors, and gallery owners to discover new talent, purchase artwork, and make deals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Venice Biennale elevates the profiles of participating artists and their countries and influences trends and conversations within the contemporary art world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Venice Biennale plays a vital role in shaping conversations within the global art community, showcasing new artists, and providing opportunities for artists to connect with galleries, collectors, and other art professionals.
- [USER] User inquired about how artists are chosen to participate in the Biennale and if it is a selective process.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The selection process for artists to participate in the Venice Biennale is highly selective, curated by a team of international curators appointed by the Biennale's board of directors.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The curatorial team invites artists from different countries and accepts artist submissions through a nomination process.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Each edition of the Biennale has a theme or concept that participating artists should reflect upon in their work, and artists submit proposals for review.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Participating in the Venice Biennale is considered a significant achievement for artists, leading to high competition for selection.
- [USER] User asked for memorable exhibits from past editions of the Venice Biennale.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 2019 Venice Biennale, the Lithuanian Pavilion featured "Sun & Sea (Marina)" by Rugilė Barzdžiukaitė, a sung-through opera about climate change.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 2013 Venice Biennale, the German Pavilion showcased "Factory" by Anne Imhof, a four-hour long performance involving performers and live animals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 2005 United States Pavilion featured "True North" by Isaac Julien, a multi-screen video piece exploring African American migration and identity.
